pins.title: Small gifts for the hiker in your life
pins.pinTitle: Small gifts for hikers: practical stocking stuffers and gift ideas for every budget
pins.description: Looking for a small gift for someone who loves the outdoors? Our hiking gift guide lists practical ideas for every budget, from printable planners to warm socks and winter gear, with what each one is good for.

pins.title: One hike a week in 2027?
pins.sub: A printable planner to keep the streak.
pins.pinTitle: 2027 hiking planner printable: hike-a-week challenge, goals and miles tracker
pins.description: Want to hike more next year? The 2027 Hiking Year Planner has a hike-a-week challenge, a place for your goals and a miles tracker. Print at home, instant download. A small gift for a hiker who likes a plan.

pins.title: For the hiker who counts every summit
pins.pinTitle: Peak bagger logbook printable: Colorado 14ers, NH 4,000-footers and Adirondack High Peaks
pins.description: A printable peak bagging log with checklists for the Colorado 14ers, the New Hampshire 4,000-footers and the Adirondack High Peaks, plus pages to record each summit. A thoughtful gift for a hiker with a list.

pins.title: Never forget the essentials again
pins.sub: Free checklist: print it before you go.
pins.pinTitle: Free hiking checklist printable: day hike essentials to pack every time
pins.description: A free printable hiking checklist with the day-hike essentials: water, food, layers, navigation, light, first aid and more. Print it, keep it by the door and tick it off before every hike.

pins.title: Hunting season? Wear blaze orange.
pins.sub: And check your state's season dates.
pins.pinTitle: Hiking during hunting season: wear blaze orange and check your state's dates
pins.description: Rifle deer seasons open in many states in November. Wear blaze orange on you and your dog, stay on marked trails and check your state wildlife agency for season dates and rules before you go. Our guide covers what to wear and where to look.

pins.title: Dark by five? Plan your winter hike.
pins.sub: See the guide: what to wear and bring.
pins.pinTitle: Winter hiking tips: plan for early dark, pack a headlamp and dress in layers
pins.description: Winter days are short, so start early, turn around with daylight to spare and always carry a headlamp with fresh batteries. Our Winter Hiking Guide shows what to wear at each temperature and has a cold-weather day-hike checklist.

pins.title: Long travel day? Pack warm socks.
pins.sub: Merino socks for planes, trains and trails.
pins.pinTitle: Merino wool socks for travel days: warm, cushioned crew socks for planes, airports and trails
pins.description: Cold airports, long drives and chilly hotel floors: a pair of merino socks makes a travel day more comfortable. Ours are 80% merino as labelled, cushioned, crew height, in four colours. Sold as one pair.

pins.title: Why so many people switch to merino
pins.sub: Warm, soft, and not just for hiking.
pins.pinTitle: Merino wool socks: are they worth it? What merino does better than cotton
pins.description: Merino wool keeps feet warmer than cotton when it gets damp and usually holds less odor, which is why people wear it at home, at work and outdoors. Our article explains when merino socks are worth it and how to care for them.

pins.title: Give a hike together, not more stuff
pins.pinTitle: Hiking gift coupons printable: an experience gift for hikers and outdoor lovers
pins.description: An experience gift for someone you love to be outside with: printable write-in coupons for hikes you will take together, a trail pass to reveal the plan and a simple planning page. Print at home, last-minute friendly.

pins.title: Seeing more than one park next year?
pins.sub: Plan the whole road trip on paper.
pins.board: Best Day Hikes in US National Parks
pins.pinTitle: National parks road trip planner printable: multi-park itinerary, reservations and budget
pins.description: Planning a road trip through several national parks? This printable planner keeps the route, day-by-day itinerary, reservation and permit tracker and budget in one place. Always check nps.gov for current entry rules.
